scenario: Greeting someone for the first time
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of Spanish

vocabulary.note: Often omitted in Spanish, but used for emphasis or clarity.
Agrees with the speaker's gender: encantado (m), encantada (f).
Used in questions; carries an accent mark.
Used for permanent characteristics, origin, and identity.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ¡Hola! Yo soy Ana. ¿Y tú?
dialogue.translation: Hello! I am Ana. And you?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Hola, Ana. Me llamo Luis. Mucho gusto.
dialogue.translation: Hello, Ana. My name is Luis. Nice to meet you.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Encantada, Luis. ¿De dónde eres?
dialogue.translation: Pleased to meet you, Luis. Where are you from?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Soy de Madrid. ¿Y tú?
dialogue.translation: I am from Madrid. And you?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Yo soy de México. ¡Muy bien! También soy de allí.
dialogue.translation: I am from Mexico. Very good! I am also from there.

key_phrases.translation: Nice to meet you (literally: much pleasure)
My name is... (literally: I call myself...)

scenario: Asking where something is in a store
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of Spanish

vocabulary.note: Indicates place near listener or farther.
Used to get attention or apologize.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Perdón, ¿dónde está el agua?
dialogue.translation: Excuse me, where is the water?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: El agua está allí, al lado de la leche.
dialogue.translation: The water is there, next to the milk.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ¿Y el pan? ¿Está aquí?
dialogue.translation: And the bread? Is it here?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sí, el pan está aquí, en la cesta.
dialogue.translation: Yes, the bread is here, in the basket.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Perfecto, busco el pan y el agua. Gracias.
dialogue.translation: Perfect, I look for the bread and the water. Thanks.

scenario: Ordering a drink at a café
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of Spanish

vocabulary.note: Common irregular verb; used for ordering politely.
Masculine noun; can also mean 'café' as a place.
Feminine noun; takes 'el' in singular for phonetic reasons.
Used idiomatically for ordering: '¿Qué te pongo?' = 'What can I get you?'
Note: already in list, but included because it's necessary? Actually avoid. I'll replace.
Feminine noun; common in café orders.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Buenos días, ¿qué quiere tomar?
dialogue.translation: Good morning, what would you like to drink?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Quiero un café con leche, por favor.
dialogue.translation: I want a coffee with milk, please.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ¿Y para beber? ¿Agua también?
dialogue.translation: And to drink? Water too?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sí, pero sin hielo, por favor.
dialogue.translation: Yes, but without ice, please.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Muy bien, le pongo el café y el agua.
dialogue.translation: Very well, I'll serve you the coffee and the water.

key_phrases.translation: What would you like to drink?
I want a coffee with milk

scenario: Buying a ticket at a station
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of Spanish

vocabulary.note: used for future plans: 'voy a...' = 'I am going to...'
also 'billete' in Spain, but 'ticket' is common in Latin America
used in questions about quantity or price
from 'costar' (to cost); used with singular nouns
used for destinations after verbs of motion
proper noun, the capital of Spain
from 'tener' (to have); used for possession or with certain expressions

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Hola, necesito un ticket para ir a Madrid.
dialogue.translation: Hello, I need a ticket to go to Madrid.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: ¿Para cuándo? ¿Ahora?
dialogue.translation: For when? Now?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Sí, ahora. ¿Cuánto cuesta?
dialogue.translation: Yes, now. How much does it cost?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: El ticket cuesta diez euros. ¿Tiene dinero?
dialogue.translation: The ticket costs ten euros. Do you have money?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Sí, tengo. Aquí tiene.
dialogue.translation: Yes, I have. Here you go.

key_phrases.phrase: un ticket para ir a Madrid
key_phrases.translation: a ticket to go to Madrid

scenario: Checking in at a hotel reception
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of Spanish

vocabulary.note: used for possession and also for age, etc.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Buenas tardes, ¿tiene una reserva?
dialogue.translation: Good afternoon, do you have a reservation?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sí, a nombre de García. Tengo una habitación para esta noche.
dialogue.translation: Yes, under the name García. I have a room for tonight.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Muy bien. ¿Me dice su nombre, por favor?
dialogue.translation: Very well. Can you tell me your name, please?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Soy María García. Gracias.
dialogue.translation: I am María García. Thank you.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Adiós, señora García.
dialogue.translation: Goodbye, Mrs. García.

scenario: Meeting a new neighbor
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of Spanish

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Hola, soy tu nuevo vecino. Vivo en el piso de al lado.
dialogue.translation: Hello, I am your new neighbor. I live in the apartment next door.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: ¡Hola! Mucho gusto. ¿Y tú? ¿Trabajas aquí cerca?
dialogue.translation: Hello! Nice to meet you. And you? Do you work near here?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Sí, trabajo en una oficina, pero mi casa está cerca.
dialogue.translation: Yes, I work in an office, but my house is close.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: ¡Qué bien! Yo vivo aquí también. ¿Te gusta tu nuevo piso?
dialogue.translation: How nice! I live here too. Do you like your new apartment?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Sí, mucho. Es un buen día para conocernos, ¿no?
dialogue.translation: Yes, a lot. It's a good day to meet, isn't it?

key_phrases.phrase: vivo en el piso de al lado
key_phrases.translation: I live in the apartment next door

scenario: Asking the time on the street
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of Spanish

vocabulary.note: Often used with 'qué' to ask the time.
Used before hours in time expressions.
Used in time expressions for minutes past the hour.
Used for minutes to the hour.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Perdón, ¿qué hora es?
dialogue.translation: Excuse me, what time is it?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Son las tres y cuarto.
dialogue.translation: It's quarter past three.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ¿Y a las cuatro menos media?
dialogue.translation: And at half past four?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: No, son las tres y media ahora.
dialogue.translation: No, it's half past three now.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Ah, gracias.
dialogue.translation: Oh, thanks.

key_phrases.translation: half past three (literally: four minus half)

scenario: At the doctor for a basic checkup
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of Spanish

vocabulary.note: Masculine noun; often used with 'el médico'.
Same form for male and female; article indicates gender.
Common in medical contexts; e.g., 'tengo dolor'.
Frequent verb; in A1 often used with 'me siento'.

dialogue.speaker: A (doctor)
dialogue.text: Buenos días, soy el médico. ¿Qué le pasa?
dialogue.translation: Good morning, I am the doctor. What is the matter with you?

dialogue.speaker: B (patient)
dialogue.text: Doctor, tengo un dolor muy fuerte en la cabeza.
dialogue.translation: Doctor, I have a very strong pain in my head.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ¿Puede abrir la boca y decir 'ah'?
dialogue.translation: Can you open your mouth and say 'ah'?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sí, me siento mal, pero puedo hacer todo.
dialogue.translation: Yes, I feel bad, but I can do everything.

key_phrases.translation: What is the matter with you? (formal)

scenario: Paying at a supermarket checkout
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of Spanish

vocabulary.note: Regular -ar verb. Used for paying at a store.
Often refers to a credit/debit card in this context.
Used to state the total amount due.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ¿Va a pagar con tarjeta o en efectivo?
dialogue.translation: Are you going to pay by card or in cash?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Voy a pagar en efectivo. ¿Cuál es el total?
dialogue.translation: I'm going to pay in cash. What is the total?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Son veinte euros. Aquí tiene su cambio y su bolsa.
dialogue.translation: It's twenty euros. Here is your change and your bag.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Muchas gracias. Y aquí tiene mi tarjeta para puntos.
dialogue.translation: Thank you very much. And here is my card for points.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Perfecto. ¿Necesita dinero en efectivo para algo más?
dialogue.translation: Perfect. Do you need cash for anything else?

key_phrases.phrase: ¿Va a pagar con tarjeta o en efectivo?
key_phrases.translation: Are you going to pay by card or in cash?

key_phrases.phrase: Aquí tiene su cambio y su bolsa.
key_phrases.translation: Here is your change and your bag.

scenario: Calling a friend to make simple plans
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of Spanish

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Hola, te llamo para hacer planes mañana.
dialogue.translation: Hi, I'm calling you to make plans for tomorrow.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sí, pero yo trabajo hasta las cinco.
dialogue.translation: Yes, but I work until five.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ¿Puedes tú después? ¿O prefieres tarde?
dialogue.translation: Can you after? Or do you prefer late?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Vale, quedamos a las seis con Ana.
dialogue.translation: Okay, we meet at six with Ana.

scenario: Describing your family to someone
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of Spanish

vocabulary.note: Possessive adjective, used before singular nouns.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Mi familia es grande: tengo dos hermanos y una hermana.
dialogue.translation: My family is big: I have two brothers and one sister.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: ¿Y tu madre y tu padre?
dialogue.translation: And your mother and your father?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Mi madre vive cerca y mi padre también.
dialogue.translation: My mother lives nearby and my father too.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: ¿Tienes una familia pequeña o grande?
dialogue.translation: Do you have a small or big family?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: No, es pequeña, pero mi hermana vive conmigo.
dialogue.translation: No, it's small, but my sister lives with me.

scenario: Asking for directions in the street
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of Spanish

vocabulary.note: Often used with 'a la' – 'a la derecha'.
Often used with 'a la' – 'a la izquierda'.
Used to indicate movement along a street.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Disculpe, ¿dónde está la calle de la derecha?
dialogue.translation: Excuse me, where is the street on the right?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Siga recto por esta calle y luego gire a la izquierda.
dialogue.translation: Go straight along this street and then turn left.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ¿Está cerca o lejos?
dialogue.translation: Is it near or far?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Está cerca. Siga recto y verá la calle.
dialogue.translation: It's near. Continue straight and you will see the street.

scenario: On a bus asking the driver for help
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of Spanish

vocabulary.note: Used to ask the driver to stop at a specific place.
Often used in questions to ask for information.
Feminine noun; used in 'pedir ayuda' (to ask for help).
Masculine noun; refers to someone riding a bus or train.
Masculine noun; for a female driver, 'conductora' is also used.
Polite request phrase; always used to be courteous.
Used to refer to the next stop, station, etc.
Used to introduce a time clause.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Perdón, conductor, tengo una pregunta.
dialogue.translation: Excuse me, driver, I have a question.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sí, pasajero, ¿en qué puedo ayudar?
dialogue.translation: Yes, passenger, how can I help?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ¿Puede parar en la siguiente parada, por favor?
dialogue.translation: Can you stop at the next stop, please?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sí, pero quiero saber cuándo va a bajar usted.
dialogue.translation: Yes, but I want to know when you are going to get off.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Voy a bajar ahora, gracias.
dialogue.translation: I'm going to get off now, thank you.

key_phrases.translation: I am going to get off

scenario: Introducing a colleague at work
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of Spanish

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Hola, te presento a Juan. Él es nuestro nuevo compañero.
dialogue.translation: Hello, let me introduce you to Juan. He is our new colleague.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: ¡Hola, Juan! Bienvenido. ¿Te gusta trabajar aquí?
dialogue.translation: Hello, Juan! Welcome. Do you like working here?

dialogue.speaker: C
dialogue.text: Sí, gracias. Me parece que vamos a trabajar bien juntos.
dialogue.translation: Yes, thank you. I think we are going to work well together.

dialogue.speaker: A

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Igualmente. El gusto es mío.
dialogue.translation: Likewise. The pleasure is mine.

scenario: Leaving a voicemail message
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of Spanish

vocabulary.note: Commonly used for leaving messages or objects.
Already in the file, but included here as it appears in the dialogue.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Hola, soy Ana. Quiero dejar un mensaje para el doctor.
dialogue.translation: Hello, I'm Ana. I want to leave a message for the doctor.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sí, dígame. ¿Puede llamar más tarde?
dialogue.translation: Yes, tell me. Can you call later?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: No, prefiero hablar ahora. Necesito una cita.
dialogue.translation: No, I prefer to speak now. I need an appointment.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Claro. ¿Puede darme su número de teléfono?
dialogue.translation: Of course. Can you give me your phone number?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Sí, es el 555-1234. Puede llamarme después de las dos.
dialogue.translation: Yes, it's 555-1234. You can call me after two.

scenario: At the post office sending a package
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of Spanish

vocabulary.note: common verb for sending mail or packages
used in questions about quantity or price

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Hola, necesito enviar este paquete.
dialogue.translation: Hello, I need to send this package.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Claro. Primero, vamos a pesar el paquete aquí.
dialogue.translation: Of course. First, we are going to weigh the package here.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ¿Cuánto cuesta enviarlo?
dialogue.translation: How much does it cost to send it?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Es muy barato, todo está bien. Pero necesita la dirección.
dialogue.translation: It is very cheap, everything is fine. But you need the address.

key_phrases.translation: I need to send this package

scenario: Describing your daily routine
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of Spanish

vocabulary.note: Reflexive verb, often used for daily routines.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ¿A qué hora te levantas por la mañana?
dialogue.translation: At what time do you get up in the morning?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Me levanto a las siete y desayuno con mi familia.
dialogue.translation: I get up at seven and have breakfast with my family.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ¿Y luego vas al trabajo?
dialogue.translation: And then do you go to work?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sí, luego trabajo, y siempre vuelvo a casa por la noche.
dialogue.translation: Yes, then I work, and I always return home at night.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Perfecto, gracias por contarme tu rutina.
dialogue.translation: Perfect, thank you for telling me your routine.

key_phrases.translation: At what time do you get up?

scenario: Asking about opening hours
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of Spanish

vocabulary.note: Past participle of 'abrir', used as adjective.
Past participle of 'cerrar', used as adjective.
Also means 'afternoon' as noun; here adverb.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ¿A qué hora abre la tienda?
dialogue.translation: At what time does the store open?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Abre a las nueve de la mañana y cierra a las seis de la tarde.
dialogue.translation: It opens at nine in the morning and closes at six in the evening.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ¿Está abierto desde el lunes hasta el sábado?
dialogue.translation: Is it open from Monday until Saturday?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sí, pero el domingo está cerrado. Y los sábados cierra más temprano.
dialogue.translation: Yes, but on Sunday it is closed. And on Saturdays it closes earlier.

key_phrases.translation: At what time does it open?

scenario: Choosing a dish from a menu
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of Spanish

vocabulary.note: Demonstrative; used to point to something near.
Irregular verb; also used in expressions like 'tener hambre' (to be hungry).
Used to ask for a selection from a set.
Stem-changing verb (e-ie); common in service contexts.
Contrast conjunction (already in file, but included for completeness? Actually avoid? Wait, it's in the list to avoid; I'll not include it.)

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Este plato tiene pollo, pero ¿cuál recomiendas?
dialogue.translation: This dish has chicken, but which one do you recommend?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Recomiendo la paella, tiene más sabor y menos grasa.
dialogue.translation: I recommend the paella, it has more flavor and less fat.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ¿Y el precio? Es el mismo para los dos.
dialogue.translation: And the price? It is the same for both.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sí, el precio es el mismo, pero la paella es mejor para comer.
dialogue.translation: Yes, the price is the same, but the paella is better to eat.

scenario: At the bank for a simple transaction
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of Spanish

vocabulary.note: Used to express desire; common in polite requests.
Masculine noun; often used with 'tener' or 'necesitar'.
Refers to bank account; also means 'bill' in other contexts.
Used to indicate exchange, cause, or duration.
As adjective means 'only' (e.g., solo quiero) or 'alone'.
Feminine noun; used for signing documents.
Used to refer to a different one.
Used to add information or agreement.

vocabulary.translation: to pass, to happen, to come in
vocabulary.note: Commonly used as 'pass me' or 'come in' in service contexts.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Buenos días, quiero sacar dinero de mi cuenta, por favor.
dialogue.translation: Good morning, I want to withdraw money from my account, please.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sí, ¿cuánto quiere sacar? Solo necesito su tarjeta y una firma.
dialogue.translation: Yes, how much do you want to withdraw? I only need your card and a signature.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Quiero cien euros. ¿Puedo pasar por otro mostrador para cambiar dinero?
dialogue.translation: I want a hundred euros. Can I go to another counter to exchange money?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Claro, también puede hacer eso allí. Aquí tiene su dinero y su firma está lista.
dialogue.translation: Of course, you can also do that there. Here is your money and your signature is ready.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Gracias, todo perfecto.
dialogue.translation: Thank you, all perfect.
